author: TEDx Talks
description:
Data centers have the earned their reputation as energy hogs. If we designed them to be more flexible, the demand load can be shaped to match the availability of clean power on the grid.
Not all computing tasks are urgent. Batch jobs, model fine-tuning, and large-scale processing can wait minutes or hours without anyone noticing. If data centers can slow down when clean energy is scarce and speed up when renewables are abundant, they stop being the enemy of the grid and become one of its most useful tools. What began as whiteboard sketches rejected by funding agencies is now running on real-world data centers. Professor Ayse Coskun is the Chief Scientist at Emerald AI, a startup focused on enabling power flexibility in data centers. She is also a full professor in the Electrical and Computer Engineering Department at Boston University, where she leads the Center for Information and Systems Engineering and serves as Associate Dean for Research at the College of Engineering. author: TEDx Talks
description: The clean energy transition has a dirty secret: it runs on metals whose supply chains are fragile, carbon-intensive, and nowhere near large enough to meet demand. Every solar panel, EV battery, and fusion reactor requires critical minerals like neodymium, cobalt, lithium, and dozens more in quantities that current mining cannot sustainably supply. Tomás Villalón Jr. argues the solution is not to dig more holes. Most of what we need is already above ground, sitting in mining waste piles, industrial byproduct streams, and discarded electronics. The key molecules were always there. We just lacked the technology to retrieve them effectively. Now that new engineering is unlocking the ability to parse these materials, the question is whether we treat the waste we have already created as the resource it is. Tomás Villalón Jr. has built his career at the intersection of materials science, clean energy supply chains, and circular economy innovation. He is the co-founder and CTO of Pheonix Tail
title: The supply chain crisis hiding inside clean energy technologies | Tomás Villalón Jr. | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description: Data centers are "hungry" and "thirsty", now how do we keep them from getting hangry? Just as we might talk about balance and optimization for human performance in the workplace, the growing fleet of digital colleagues can work smarter, not harder. How we design and operate these tools greatly affects the efficiency. One video generation request produces five times as much carbon as a single text query, and adding a sentence to an AI prompt can reduce its resource demand by up to half. A data center in Arizona running on coal power is a fundamentally different environmental proposition than one in Finland cooling with surrounding seawater and batching jobs when renewable energy peaks. Sustainable computing approaches extend the value and capacity of our digital infrastructure.  Yankai (Luke) Jiang is a PhD researcher in computer science focused on sustainable data center design, with particular expertise in the environmental tradeoffs between carbon emissions and water consumption in
title: How you write an AI prompt dramatically changes its carbon footprint | Yankai Jiang | TEDxBoston

That eliminates most cities, small islands, mountain communities, and disaster relief zones from the map. What if we rethought the conventional turbine?

離開外商銀行的高薪工作後，郭雅芸開始重新定義夢想：它不是單一形狀，而是一塊塊拼圖組成的人生。
那些看似平凡的部分——財務安全、健康、家庭、休息——都和舞台一樣重要。
做自己，不是任性，而是清楚選擇並勇敢承擔；而夢想的真相，其實就是接納不完美的自己，拼出屬於自己的人生圖樣。
 郭雅芸（Shania），政大金融系碩士，曾任職於外商金融業十四年，自金融業踏入烘焙創作領域。
因熱愛烘焙毅然轉換跑道，從業餘麵包創作出發，逐步打造個人品牌「辣媽Shania」，擅長將麵包結合創意與故事行銷，於社群平台累積近四十幾萬名粉絲。
她不僅經營自媒體，也積極跨界合作，持續為夢想努力，從麵包設計、出書成為作家到演講分享，致力於鼓勵更多人突破框架、擁抱熱情。
其真誠與幽默的風格深受觀眾喜愛，是結合創業精神與熱愛生命的代表人物。 This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

In this powerful talk, Rebekah explores how silence becomes rudeness, difference becomes threat, and uncertainty becomes assumption. Drawing from moments of grief, social pressure, and mislabeling, she reveals how easily we confuse what we see for who someone is. This talk is an invitation to change perspective, stay with the discomfort of not knowing, and discover the full spectrum of humanity hidden just beyond first glance. title: Second Chances: The Fine Art Of Starting Over | Rebekah Dawt Thachin | TEDxUCIS Youth

This talk reveals how stripping away noise allows us to truly sense the world. Discover how observing the ordinary transforms personal creativity into a powerful, shared force for collective care. Nixsa (Nixsa Saenjaibal) is a multidisciplinary Thai artist, singer-songwriter, and producer who views creativity as a "way of living" rather than a talent. Her work is deeply rooted in sensory perception and cultural fusion, often utilizing unique  and traditional instruments to bridge boundaries. From her classical roots to modern sound comfort, she treats creativity as a "shared force" to respond to her community, emphasizing that true perception—and even silence—serves as a powerful tool for meaningful, collective care. description: What if dressing to blend in is actually erasing who you are? This talk explores the exhausting pressure of viral trends and the power of "style as resistance." By embracing family heritage and the art of sewing, discover how true confidence isn't bought—it's designed. It’s time to fire "Trends." Elly is on a mission to "fire trends" as her personal stylist. Her journey from crafting spiky silver bracelets to sewing custom dresses explores the pressures and joys of modern youth culture. She draws inspiration from vintage family archives and the underground music scene to navigate her unique identity. Ultimately, Elly believes the most powerful thing you can wear is your own truth. description: What if a single connection could save your life? Gripping and deeply personal, this talk links our biology to our deepest search for meaning. By debunking the "lone wolf" myth and introducing the "Triangle of Connection," discover how mastering risk, intention, and trust builds the ultimate foundation for human resilience. Ella is an international student in Chiang Mai, Thailand. Her passion for the connecting with people was initially sparked by her curiosity about human nature and the role of relationships in our lives. This curiosity later inspired her to develop her own theory, called “the triangle of connection,” which explains how individuals and society can achieve more together. author: TEDx Talks
description: Society tells us feeling lost is a failure, but what if it’s a necessary reorientation? Through personal stories of immigration and travel, this talk flips the script on uncertainty. Discover why losing your map—and stepping off the planned path—might just be the most powerful compass you have for authentic self-discovery. Meet Crystal, a 15 year-old student who moved from Shanghai, China to study in Chiang Mai, Thailand at a young age. She lived a fast-paced life in a Chinese school system, but once she moved to Thailand, she was thrown into lessons entirely in English which left her feeling alienated and lost. Crystal brings a unique perspective to the TEDxUCIS Youth Event, where she will speak about how the sensation of feeling lost is not a failure but a gateway to discovering our authentic self, new opportunities and new potentials. title: Why Being Lost Is Your Best Compass | Niu (Crystal) Yue Yue | TEDxUCIS Youth

If you're tired of pointless meetings, shallow conversations, and feeling unheard, this talk is your turning point. It is your chance to unlock the hidden genius in yourself and everyone around you. It reveals simple ways of being with one another which transformed the approach of a failing company in just 37 minutes, helped a 10-year-old boy overcome anxiety attacks, and enhanced respect, connection and affinity in a partner relationship. These simple behaviours have the power to deepen any relationship in your life. They rest on giving full attention and promising not to interrupt.
